subject.title: [Bug]: /v1/responses client tools are dropped by the native Codex app-server harness

question: Should a caller-provided `/v1/responses` function invocation be a terminal delegated event in the native Codex app-server harness, with the harness settling the dynamic-tool RPC but neither executing the function locally nor allowing a follow-on assistant response?
rationale: The observable omission is well described, but the correct Codex protocol response and stop ordering define a durable ownership boundary between the caller, OpenClaw, and the app-server runtime.

options.title: Adopt terminal delegation
options.body: Specify that validated caller functions are ephemeral Codex tools whose invocation is recorded as a delegated HTTP function call and terminates the turn without local execution.

options.title: Keep Codex unsupported
options.body: Document that native Codex agents cannot serve caller-provided `/v1/responses` tools and retain the current fail-closed response.

options.title: Design a broader dynamic-tool contract
options.body: Pause this narrow repair until a reusable Codex dynamic-tool lifecycle API defines delegated calls and terminal results for other callers.

recommendation.title: Adopt terminal delegation
recommendation.body: Specify that validated caller functions are ephemeral Codex tools whose invocation is recorded as a delegated HTTP function call and terminates the turn without local execution.

likelyOwner.reason: The merged adjacent client-tool forwarding work provides the clearest available ownership trail into the affected request pipeline, though Codex-extension ownership should be confirmed during maintainer review.
